candidates.topic: The Mary Celeste — Abandoned Ship Found Sailing Perfectly
candidates.teaser: A ship was found in the middle of the ocean — crew gone, food still warm, no sign of struggle.
candidates.video_title: The Ship Found Sailing With No One Aboard
candidates.video_description: In 1872, the Mary Celeste was discovered drifting in the Atlantic fully intact — cargo untouched, food on the table, lifeboat missing. No crew was ever found. The mystery remains unsolved to this day.
candidates.script: A fully loaded ship was found sailing perfectly through the Atlantic — no one on board, food still on the table, cargo untouched. In 1872, the Mary Celeste had vanished crew and zero signs of struggle. The lifeboat was missing but no bodies were ever recovered. Nine people disappeared in calm weather, in the middle of nowhere. So — did they jump, or were they taken?

candidates.topic: Tetrachromacy — Women Who See Millions More Colors
candidates.teaser: Some people can see colors that literally do not exist for the rest of us — and most of them don't even know it.
candidates.video_title: Some Humans Can See Colors You Never Will
candidates.video_description: Most humans have three color receptors in their eyes. A rare group of women carry four — giving them the ability to perceive up to 100 million distinct colors. The average person sees around one million. Scientists call this tetrachromacy.
candidates.script: Right now, some women are seeing colors that your brain is physically incapable of processing. Most humans have three color receptors — they can see about one million colors. Tetrachromats have four, unlocking up to 100 million shades. That's entire spectrums invisible to you. Scientists estimate roughly 12% of women carry this mutation. The wild part? Most of them have never realized they see differently. Do you think you might be one?

candidates.teaser: In 1977, a radio telescope picked up a signal so unusual that a scientist scrawled one word next to it — and we've never heard it again.
candidates.video_title: The 72-Second Signal That Might Be Alien
candidates.video_description: On August 15, 1977, astronomer Jerry Ehman detected a radio burst so perfectly matching the expected profile of alien communication that he circled it and wrote 'Wow!' in the margin. It lasted exactly 72 seconds and has never been detected again.
candidates.script: On August 15th, 1977, a radio telescope in Ohio picked up a signal so bizarre that the astronomer monitoring it circled the printout and wrote one word: Wow. It lasted exactly 72 seconds, matched every theoretical profile for an extraterrestrial transmission, then vanished. Decades of scanning the same patch of sky — total silence. No natural explanation has ever been confirmed. Was it a glitch, or did someone answer back?

candidates.topic: The Placebo Surgery — Fake Operations That Actually Worked
candidates.teaser: Doctors performed a surgery, cut patients open, then sewed them back up without doing anything — and the patients got better.
candidates.video_title: Fake Surgeries That Genuinely Healed Patients
candidates.video_description: In controlled trials, surgeons have performed sham operations — making incisions, then closing without any real procedure — and patients reported the same pain relief as those who received real surgery. The placebo effect is powerful enough to mimic the knife.
candidates.script: Surgeons cut patients open, did absolutely nothing, then sewed them back up. Those patients reported the exact same recovery as people who had real surgery. This wasn't an accident — it was a controlled trial. In multiple knee and back studies, sham operations matched real procedures in pain relief. Your brain, believing it was fixed, physically repaired itself. The most powerful drug ever tested might be the human mind. Does that change how you see medicine?

candidates.teaser: Scientists just thawed something that's been frozen for nearly 50,000 years — and it immediately came back to life.
candidates.video_description: In 2022, French scientists successfully reactivated a virus extracted from Siberian permafrost that had been frozen for 48,500 years. As global temperatures rise and permafrost melts, ancient pathogens humanity has never encountered — and has no immunity to — could re-enter circulation.
candidates.script: Scientists thawed a 48,500-year-old virus from Siberian permafrost — and it was still alive. In 2022, French researchers reactivated multiple ancient pathogens frozen since before modern humans existed. Here's the problem: as the planet warms, permafrost is melting globally, releasing viruses our immune systems have never encountered in all of recorded history. We have zero immunity. Scientists say this isn't hypothetical. It's already happening. How worried should we actually be?
